diet.text: Lizards, snakes, rodents, birds, frogs and insects

overview.text: The Coachwhip is a long, very fast, non-venomous snake of the southern United States and northern Mexico. Its tail scales look like the braids of a leather whip.

identification.text: Thin body, small head and big eyes with round pupils. Colour varies with the soil it lives on - tan with darker flecks, dark brown to black, or even pink in parts of west Texas.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Across the southern United States from coast to coast, and the northern half of Mexico.

habitat.text: Open, sandy places: pine woods, old fields, prairies, sandhill scrub and coastal dunes.

behaviour.text: Active by day, alert and quick to flee - it can move at up to about 6 km/h. It sometimes lifts its head above the grass to look around. If cornered it strikes; the bite hurts but is harmless. Coachwhips roam over some of the largest home ranges known for any snake.

diet.text: A fast hunter that eats almost anything it can catch: other snakes, lizards, frogs, rodents, birds and their eggs, and insects such as cicadas.

funfacts.text: Coachwhips sometimes 'periscope' - lifting their heads high above the grass to look around.

recognise.text: Big eyes and a small head.
